name: session-name-control-bytes-escaped
description: The control-byte guard applies to session-name exactly as it does to cwd: the producer escapes a newline (%0A), the reader decodes, sees a control byte, and refuses the value — name lands empty rather than carrying a raw newline.
grounding: The control-byte guard is a property of the decoder, not of one field: a decoded cwd OR session-name containing any C0 control (< 0x20) or DEL (0x7F) is refused and stored empty, never as raw bytes.
notes: The cwd half of this rule was already pinned by cwd-control-bytes-escaped; the session-name half was not, so a reader could have guarded cwd alone and kept the corpus green. Session names are the likelier injection vector of the two — they are user-supplied free text, where a cwd comes from the filesystem. Lossy on purpose, so it keeps encode_from.
